title: Research
text: My research develops learning and signal-processing methods for data with relational and multi-domain structure. I am particularly interested in methods that combine mathematical structure, scalable learning, and interpretable representations.

title: Research
text:
Research directions

Graph machine learning and graph neural networks
I study learning architectures for graph-structured data, with emphasis on principled graph filters, continuous formulations, scalability, stability, and the behavior of deep graph models.


Graph signal processing and graph learning
A central theme of my work is learning graph structure from observed signals and exploiting graph spectral structure for inference, forecasting, source separation, and representation learning.


Higher-order and multi-domain structures
My recent research extends graph learning beyond pairwise interactions to product graphs, simplicial complexes, hypergraphs, and related higher-order structures. This includes continuous product and simplicial neural networks.


Generative models
I am interested in connecting structured signal models with modern generative learning, including flow-based methods for spatiotemporal and graph-structured data.


Biomedical and spatiotemporal applications
Applications include brain and EEG signals, seizure analysis, sleep staging, weather and traffic forecasting, and other biomedical signal and image problems.

title: Aref Einizade
text:
Graph machine learning · Signal processing · Higher-order structures
  
  Assistant Professor at Télécom SudParis, Institut Polytechnique de Paris
  
    
      I am an Assistant Professor at Télécom SudParis, Institut Polytechnique de Paris. I joined Télécom SudParis in February 2026 after a postdoctoral position in the Multimedia team at Télécom Paris, where I worked with Jhony H. Giraldo and Fragkiskos D. Malliaros.
      My research lies at the intersection of graph machine learning, graph signal processing, and graph neural networks. I develop theoretically grounded methods for multi-domain and higher-order relational structures, with applications including biomedical data and brain signals, weather, traffic forecasting, and emerging generative-model settings.
      I received my PhD in Electrical Engineering from Sharif University of Technology in 2023. My doctoral research focused on subspace identification and graph learning of graph signals, especially for brain-signal processing. My recent work extends these ideas to simplicial complexes, hypergraphs, and continuous graph-learning models.
